answer: In an attestation graph, bounded random walks propagate trust without allowing influence to grow unchecked with path length. Under a normalized walk, a sybil cluster joined to the honest graph by a sparse cut has low conductance, limiting its reachable voting mass; min-cut and transitivity bounds make dense internal attestations insufficient. Whether framed as a relic of endorsements, a karst-like hidden channel, or a mirror network, it must earn cross-cluster links to escape that bound.
